messages:
perf-bot: CI microbench alert: PR #21011 failed threshold checks on `batcher_kv_warmup` (median latency +12.1% vs baseline, threshold 5%). KV cache hit rate down 7.4%. Full report: https://ci.redwood/internal/bench/21011 :warning:

maria: saw this when I woke up, noticed the kernel-autoselect tweak merged in 0c1a2b broke affinity for short sequences. :eyes:

koji: thanks — starting a quick bisect on the post-merge range now. suspecting the prefetch/eviction heuristic refactor (d34f9..). will post results in ~30m.

alex: I can repro locally with the same seed. running: ```./tools/run_microbench --suite=batcher_kv_warmup --repeat=200 --seed=2026 --kv-debug``` will attach flamegraph.

perf-bot: attached metric snapshot (excerpt): ```kv_hit_rate: baseline=0.82 -> pr=0.759
median_latency_ms: baseline=11.4 -> pr=12.8
95p_latency_ms: baseline=28.3 -> pr=33.1```

sasha: if bisect confirms, this is a rollout blocker for the dedicated rollout tomorrow. we should plan a revert unless we have a targeted fix in <2 hours.

koji: bisect update: narrowed to commit d34f9c1 -> d34f9c1 modifies `prefetch_window` and kernel selection boundary. repro runs show kv_hit_rate drops only when kernel-autoselect picks larger kernel for batch sizes < 8.

maria: that matches the heatmap: kernel_assignments shifted from kernel_v2_small -> kernel_v2_medium for short requests. looks like our cost model underestimated small-token path.

alex: quick patch idea: clamp kernel choice for seq_len <= 32 to prefer small kernels while we investigate. testing patch now.```git apply <<PATCH
*** Begin Patch
*** Update: runtime/kernel_selector.py
@@
-    if estimated_throughput[medium] > estimated_throughput[small]:
-        return 'medium'
+    # temporary clamp: avoid medium kernel for very short sequences to keep KV hit locality
+    if seq_len <= 32:
+        return 'small'
+    if estimated_throughput[medium] > estimated_throughput[small]:
+        return 'medium'
*** End Patch
```

sasha: good. two paths: A) revert merge 0c1a2b and unblock rollout, B) hotfix PR with clamp and run CI. which is faster?

maria: revert will be fastest to unblock. hotfix PR will need cross-checks but could be merged if CI passes in ~20-30m. I'm for revert + follow-up patch.

koji: bisect final: d34f9c1 is root cause. test harness: `tools/bench_driver --ci --profile=kvcache,autoselect --runs=50` reproduces the delta consistently.

alex: my local with clamp patch: kv_hit_rate back to 0.819, median latency 11.6ms — within noise. pushing hotfix branch `pr-21011-clamp-kernel`.

perf-bot: CI triggered for `pr-21011-clamp-kernel` (job 98765). running microbench suites. will post pass/fail.

maria: I'm creating revert PR for 0c1a2b now to unblock the rollout, assigning @sasha for approval.

sasha: ack. will approve revert once CI for revert commit is green. also agree we should follow with a targeted fix and expanded microbench coverage for short-sequence kernel decisions. :thumbsup:

alex: attaching flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/21011-clamp -- shows hotloop time went down in selector hop.

koji: next steps: 1) merge revert to unblock, 2) land clamp hotfix if its CI green, 3) add unit + microbench for seq_len <=64 case, 4) re-evaluate kernel cost model. I'll open a bisect PR with the repro harness and findings.

maria: thanks all. tracking in issue: https://issues.redwood/PR-21011-regress. will update CHANGES and notify release.

perf-bot: CI for `pr-21011-clamp-kernel` passed microbench suites (job 98765) — latency within baseline thresholds.

sasha: since hotfix CI is green, don't need revert if we can get fast review. maria, do you want me to approve hotfix instead?

maria: please approve hotfix and skip revert. going to run a small canary once merged.

koji: +1. will follow up with a postmortem and add a golden test for kernel-autoselect on small seqs.

alex: merging hotfix now. thanks team. :rocket:
